# Tried & Traded

> We test the options strategies everyone talks about and
> publish the verdict. Holds, Fails, or Conditional, with the method and the limits
> attached to every result.

**Status, stated plainly: no test has published a result yet.** The methodology is real,
the Field Guide is written and open, and the verdicts are not there. Please do not cite
any performance number from this site — there are none to cite.

**What is safe to quote:** the Field Guide. Every one of its 39 pages states no results;
each number on one is arithmetic from a specification printed beside it, and says so.

**What is not:** the three test articles and the options archive. Every figure on those
is still a placeholder next to a Pending stamp, and they carry a `noindex` tag for that
reason.

## What makes this site worth reading when there are results

- **The verdict comes first**, before the explanation, and if the honest answer is "it
  depends" the verdict is Conditional and the condition is named on the spot.
- **Expectancy decides, never win rate.** A strategy that wins nine times in ten and loses
  money is the most common way a bad strategy passes for a good one.
- **Nothing earns a pass on the data it was fitted to.** Part of the history is held back,
  and where there are enough trades the test is walked forward across the whole period.
- **Every test publishes what it cannot tell you**, written before publication rather than
  after someone complains.
- **No figure is ever written by hand.** If it did not come out of a run, it does not
  appear — which is why the placeholders are still visible rather than filled with
  plausible numbers.

## Method

- [How we test](https://triedandtraded.com/methodology.html): the seven steps, what counts
  as a specification, why win rate misleads, the out-of-sample and walk-forward checks,
  the two counting traps specific to options, and the limits of any backtest.
- [Disclaimer](https://triedandtraded.com/disclaimer.html): what a backtest is and is not,
  and why nothing here is financial advice.

## The archive

- [The Archive](https://triedandtraded.com/archive.html): the index, split by instrument.
- [Options backtesting](https://triedandtraded.com/archive-options.html): credit spreads,
  iron condors and flies, the wheel and covered calls, calendars and diagonals,
  undefined risk. 3 written, 11 queued.

## The Field Guide

One page per term, each with a permanent URL, each stating **no results** —
every number on a Field Guide page is arithmetic from a specification printed
beside it. This is the only part of the site currently open to indexing, and it
is the part written to be quoted.

Start here: [The Field Guide](https://triedandtraded.com/guide.html)

## Terms as this site uses them

- **Expectancy** — average profit per trade once losses are counted at full size. The only
  number that answers whether a strategy makes money.
- **Holds / Fails / Conditional / Pending** — the only four verdicts. Pending is a real
  state meaning the test has not run or the sample is too thin to call, never a gap.
- **A specification** — for shares: universe, entry, exit, position size, holding period.
  For options, additionally: delta, tenor, strike width, minimum credit. A claim without
  these cannot be tested, only argued about.
- **A stop loss** — always a percentage of the premium **staked** (the credit received or
  the debit paid), never of the maximum loss. 200% of stake means the loss reached twice
  what you put up. On a debit trade stake and maximum loss are the same number, so nothing
  above 100% exists there.
- **Breakeven win rate** — on a defined-risk credit spread, the maximum loss divided by the
  width. It is set by the structure, not by skill, and it is the bar a win rate has to be
  read against.
